memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After the Lord your God has driven them out before you, do not say to yourself, "The Lord has brought me here to take possession of this land because of my righteousness." No, it is on account of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord is going to drive them out before you. It is not because of your righteousness or your integrity that you are going to take possession of their land; but on account of the wickedness of these nations, the Lord your God will drive them out before you, to accomplish what he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. - Deut 9:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses says something Israel needed to hear, and so do we. When they entered the land and enjoyed God's blessing, they would be tempted to think, "God gave us this because we deserved it. We earned this by our goodness." Moses cuts that thought off firmly, and repeats it so they cannot miss it: "It is not because of your righteousness." God was acting because of the wickedness of the nations being judged, and because of His own faithful promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — not because Israel had earned anything.

This strikes at the root of a pride that lives in every human heart: the belief that God's blessings are our reward for being good. It feels natural to think this way. When life goes well, we assume we deserved it; when we receive grace, we quietly credit our own worthiness. But God will not let His people rest on that illusion. Everything they received was grace, rooted in His promise and His character, not their merit.

This is the very heart of the gospel. We are not saved, blessed, or brought into God's family because of our righteousness — "not by works, so that no one can boast" (Eph 2:9). Salvation rests entirely on God's grace and His faithful promise, fulfilled in Christ. This truth humbles our pride and, at the same time, gives us unshakable security. If God's favor depended on our goodness, we could never be sure of it. But because it rests on His grace, it is certain. You are here by grace, not merit. Let that both humble and steady you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I secretly believe God blesses me because I deserve it?
- How does "not because of your righteousness" both humble me and give me security?
- Where do I need to rest in grace rather than my own goodness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the pride that thinks I have earned Your blessing. Everything I have is grace, rooted in Your promise and fulfilled in Christ, not in my own goodness. Humble my heart and let me rest secure in Your unearned grace. Amen.
